title: Rankings and Positions
subtopics: Rank from top and rank from bottom
learningGoals: Convert rank from top to rank from bottom using the total formula
Find the total number of students when both top and bottom ranks are given
Calculate the number of people between two students in a row
Determine position from the right end in a row given column and total columns
Rank a name alphabetically in a given list
coreIdeas: Rank from top + Rank from bottom − 1 = Total students (the student is counted only once)
People between two students = Total − Rank from left − Rank from right (when counted from opposite ends)
Position from right = Total columns − Column number + 1
Alphabetical ranking: sort names A to Z and count the position
When new students join above someone, their rank from top increases by the number of new students

workedExamples.problem: Riya is 5th from the top in a class of 30. What is her rank from the bottom?
workedExamples.solution: Rank from bottom = Total − Rank from top + 1 = 30 − 5 + 1 = 26.
workedExamples.concept: Converting rank from top to rank from bottom

workedExamples.problem: Arjun is 8th from the top and 12th from the bottom. How many students are there in total?
workedExamples.solution: Total = Rank from top + Rank from bottom − 1 = 8 + 12 − 1 = 19.

workedExamples.problem: Priya is 6th from the left and Raj is 4th from the right in a row of 15. How many people sit between them?
workedExamples.solution: People between = Total − Rank from left − Rank from right = 15 − 6 − 4 = 5.
workedExamples.concept: People between two students in a row

workedExamples.problem: A student sits in column 4 out of 8 columns. What is their position from the right?
workedExamples.solution: Position from right = Total columns − Column number + 1 = 8 − 4 + 1 = 5.

workedExamples.problem: Rank PRIYA among: AMIT, MEERA, PRIYA, RAHUL, SANA in alphabetical order.
workedExamples.solution: Alphabetical order: AMIT (1st), MEERA (2nd), PRIYA (3rd), RAHUL (4th), SANA (5th). PRIYA is ranked 3rd.

onboarding.hook: Who is first? Who is last? Who is in the middle? Ranking questions are everywhere in exams — and one formula cracks most of them!
onboarding.avatarIntro: Hi! I am Spark. Today we tackle ranking questions — the type where you are told someone is 5th from the top and need to find their rank from the bottom. Sounds tricky? One formula makes it instant!
onboarding.priorKnowledge: You already know how to count positions in a queue. Today we formalise that into a formula and extend it to rows, columns, and alphabetical lists.

sessionFlow.subtopic: Rank from Top — Converting to Rank from Bottom
sessionFlow.coachHook: One student, two ranks — one from the top, one from the bottom. They are linked by the total!

boardDemo.title: Riya is 5th from top in class of 30. Find her rank from bottom.
steps: Draw a vertical list of 30 students
Riya is at position 5 from the top
Formula: Rank from bottom = Total − Rank from top + 1
Riya is 26th from the bottom
boardDemo.teacherLine: Why +1? Because Riya herself is included in both counts. Without +1, we would leave her out. Always use: Total − Rank + 1.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Riya is 5th from the top in a class of 30. Rank from bottom = 30 − 5 + 1 = 26.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Sam is 7th from the top in a class of 25. What is his rank from the bottom?  (a) 18  (b) 19  (c) 17  (d) 20
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! 25 − 7 + 1 = 19. Sam is 19th from the bottom. Formula applied perfectly!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Use: Total − Rank from top + 1 = 25 − 7 + 1 = 19. The +1 accounts for Sam himself.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Write the formula for rank from bottom given rank from top and total.

sessionFlow.coachHook: If you know rank from top AND rank from bottom, you can find the total in one step!

boardDemo.title: Arjun is 8th from top and 12th from bottom. Find total students.
steps: Formula: Total = Rank from top + Rank from bottom − 1
Verify: 19 − 8 + 1 = 12 from bottom. Correct!
boardDemo.teacherLine: The formula subtracts 1 because Arjun is counted in BOTH his top rank and his bottom rank. Without subtracting 1, he gets counted twice.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Total = rank from top + rank from bottom − 1 = 8 + 12 − 1 = 19.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Priya is 6th from top and 14th from bottom. Total students?  (a) 20  (b) 19  (c) 21  (d) 18
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! 6 + 14 − 1 = 19. Total is 19 students. You have nailed the core formula!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Total = 6 + 14 − 1 = 19. Do not forget the −1, otherwise you count Priya twice.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Why do we subtract 1 in the total formula?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Two students stand in the same row but different spots. How many people are between them?

boardDemo.title: Priya is 6th from left, Raj is 4th from right. Row of 15. People between?
steps: Draw a row of 15 positions
Mark Priya at position 6 from left
Mark Raj at position 4 from right
People between = Total − left rank − right rank
boardDemo.teacherLine: Shortcut: Total − left rank − right rank = people between, when the two students are counted from opposite ends.

sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Amit is 5th from left, Riya is 3rd from right in a row of 20. People between them?  (a) 12  (b) 13  (c) 11  (d) 10
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Excellent! 20 − 5 − 3 = 12 people between Amit and Riya.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: People between = Total − left rank − right rank = 20 − 5 − 3 = 12.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Does this formula work if both students are counted from the same end?

sessionFlow.coachHook: When new students join above someone, their rank from top goes up!

boardDemo.title: Riya was 5th from top. 3 new students join above her. New rank?
steps: Originally Riya was 5th from top
3 new students are added above her
Each new student pushes Riya down by 1
New rank from top = 5 + 3 = 8
boardDemo.teacherLine: New students joining above push everyone below them down. Add the number of new entrants to the current top rank.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Riya was 5th. 3 new students join above her. New rank = 5 + 3 = 8.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Sam was 4th from top. 5 new students join above him. What is his new rank?  (a) 9  (b) 1  (c) 5  (d) 10
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! 4 + 5 = 9. Sam is now 9th from the top.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: New students above push Sam's rank up. 4 + 5 = 9.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: If 2 students leave from above Riya (now 8th), what is her new rank?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Clues given one by one — build the order step by step!

boardDemo.title: 5 students: A, B, C, D, E. A is 2nd, C is 4th, B is just before C.
steps: Place certain positions first: A is 2nd, C is 4th
B is just before C, so B is 3rd
Remaining positions 1st and 5th go to D and E
Possible order: D A B C E
boardDemo.teacherLine: Place the certain positions first, then use relative clues to fill the rest. Draw blank slots and fill them in order.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: A is 2nd, C is 4th, B is just before C so B is 3rd. The order is _ A B C _.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: In a row of 5: P is 3rd. Q is just after P. R is 1st. Find Q's position.  (a) 2nd  (b) 4th  (c) 5th  (d) 1st
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! P is 3rd, Q is just after P, so Q is 4th.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: P is 3rd. Q is just AFTER P — one position further down = 4th.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Write out the full order R _ P Q _ using the given clues.

sessionFlow.coachHook: The alphabet is the world's oldest ranking system. Let's use it!

boardDemo.title: Rank PRIYA among: AMIT, MEERA, PRIYA, RAHUL, SANA
steps: Sort alphabetically by first letter: A, M, P, R, S
AMIT → A (1st), MEERA → M (2nd), PRIYA → P (3rd)
RAHUL → R (4th), SANA → S (5th)
PRIYA is ranked 3rd
boardDemo.teacherLine: When first letters differ, sort by first letter. If two names share the same first letter, compare the second letter.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Alphabetical order: AMIT, MEERA, PRIYA, RAHUL, SANA. PRIYA is 3rd.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Rank KIRAN among: ANIL, DEEPA, KIRAN, MOHAN, SURESH.  (a) 2nd  (b) 3rd  (c) 4th  (d) 1st
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! ANIL, DEEPA, KIRAN, MOHAN, SURESH. KIRAN is 3rd alphabetically.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Sort by first letter: A, D, K, M, S. KIRAN starts with K — that is the 3rd position.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: If BHANU is added to the list, what rank does KIRAN move to?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Seats have two coordinates — row and column. Let's find position from the right end!

boardDemo.title: Student sits in row 3, column 4. 8 columns total. Position from right?
steps: Total columns = 8, Student is in column 4
Formula: Position from right = Total columns − Column + 1
The student is 5th from the right in row 3
boardDemo.teacherLine: This is the same formula as rank from bottom. The +1 avoids leaving the student uncounted.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Position from right = Total columns − Column + 1 = 8 − 4 + 1 = 5.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: A student sits in column 3 of a row with 10 columns. Position from right?  (a) 7  (b) 8  (c) 6  (d) 9
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! 10 − 3 + 1 = 8. The student is 8th from the right.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Position from right = 10 − 3 + 1 = 8. Same formula as rank from bottom!
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: A student is 6th from both the left and right. How many columns are there?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Three students, three ranks — who is in the middle position?

boardDemo.title: A is 3rd, B is 7th, C is 5th from top. Who is in the middle?
steps: Sort ranks numerically: 3 (A), 5 (C), 7 (B)
Middle rank = 5 → middle student = C
boardDemo.teacherLine: Sort the three ranks numerically. The middle value belongs to the middle student.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Sort ranks: 3, 5, 7. Middle rank is 5. That is student C.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: P is 2nd from top, Q is 8th, R is 5th. Who is the middle student?  (a) P  (b) R  (c) Q  (d) Cannot determine
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! Ranks sorted: 2, 5, 8. Middle rank = 5 = student R.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Sort the three ranks: 2, 5, 8. The middle rank is 5, which belongs to R.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: If a 4th student S joins at rank 6, who is now the 2nd from the top among these four?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Final speed round! Four types of ranking in quick succession. Identify the type and apply the right formula!

boardDemo.title: Ranking Speed Strategy
steps: Type 1 (top to bottom): Rank_bottom = Total − Rank_top + 1
Type 2 (find total): Total = Rank_top + Rank_bottom − 1
Type 3 (people between): Total − Left − Right
Type 4 (row-column): Total_cols − Col + 1
boardDemo.teacherLine: Four formulas, four seconds each. Practice until they are automatic!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Identify the type from the question, recall the formula, substitute, solve.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Meera is 9th from the top and 6th from the bottom of a queue. How many people are in the queue?  (a) 14  (b) 15  (c) 16  (d) 13
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Total = rank from top + rank from bottom − 1 = 9 + 6 − 1 = 14.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Write all four ranking formulas from memory.
